title: Measure a foot on a Brannock device: heel seated in the heel cup, width bar and arch pointer slid in to touch it
instruction: Measure the foot model with the Brannock device: get its heel seated in the heel cup, bring the width bar against the side of the foot and the arch pointer to the ball joint, then let go of everything.
context: Most people have had a foot measured on a Brannock device in a shoe shop (the maker says over a million have been sold). Its instructions: the heel "properly located against the back of the heel cup, by grasping the customer's ankle and device together"; "Slide the pointer ... forward so the inside curve of the pointer fits the ball joint of the foot"; "Slide the width bar firmly to the edge of the foot." Here a rigid true-size foot model stands 25 mm too far forward. The hand skill is light contact on curved anatomy: draw the heel back into the cup, then slide two small sliders (tabs 1 to 2 cm) until each just touches a bulge of the foot, without shoving the light, loose foot out of place. A hard shove on the pointer turns the foot about the cup and the rib rides past the ball joint: an arch reading about two sizes long. One hand may steady the ankle meanwhile, as the maker says; one hand can also do it alone with gentle pushes.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top. (1) Brannock device (men's), loose, 0.80 kg: metal plate 34.6 x 13.0 cm, 1 cm thick, x 0.2 to 34.8, y -6.5 to 6.5, heel cups at the far end; the back of the right heel cup (25 mm wall, inner radius 35 mm) at x 34.0, y 0. Width bar (blue) on the +y side, x 10.5 to 20.5, inner face at y 5.8 (widest), slides toward -y (0.5 N track friction), finger tab 20 x 12 x 35 mm at x 11.5. Arch pointer (blue) on the -y edge, rib (8 mm round) reaching to y -4.4 at x 20.0 (slid back), thumb tab 10 x 14 x 30 mm at x 13.0, slides along x (0.4 N). (2) Rigid foot-and-ankle display model, right foot, men's US 9, loose, 0.30 kg: 26.2 cm long, 10.0 cm wide at the ball, ankle stump 66 mm round and 14 cm tall; standing on the plate on the centre line, toes toward the robot, heel back at x 31.5 (25 mm in front of the cup's back). Both arms at the ready pose, grippers open. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Taken at the end of the run, nothing latched. 0.3: heel seated (heel's back within 3 mm of the cup's back, centred within 3 mm, foot turned under 3 deg and tilted under 3 deg). +0.3 (only with the heel seated): width bar touching the foot (contact force 0.05 to 5 N, mean over 0.5 s). +0.3 (only with the heel seated): arch pointer touching the foot (0.05 to 5 N) with its rib within 5 mm of where it meets the ball joint of the seated foot (the model's arch reading). 1.0 (success, held 1 s): all three, every finger point 2 cm or more from the foot and both sliders, and everything still (under 1 mm in 1 s). Doing nothing scores 0. Real trial, from a photo and the video: a 3 mm feeler does not fit behind the heel; a paper strip between the bar and the foot is held; the rib touches the ball joint within 5 mm of its place for this model (marked once on the device's edge); hands clear.
reset_notes: Slide the width bar to its widest and the arch pointer back; stand the foot on the centre line with its heel 25 mm in front of the back of the right heel cup; put the device back at its marked place. Simulation: each trial starts the simulator afresh.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 20 Hz control. No person: a rigid display foot stands in for a customer's foot (it does not spread under weight and moves when pushed). The foot is boxes, cylinders, capsules and spheres; its 0.30 kg, the device's 0.80 kg and the sliders' track friction (0.4, 0.5 N) are estimates. Sliders meet the foot through a compliant contact (3 N/mm) for the vinyl skin. The toe-length reading is not part of the task; width and arch scales are not drawn.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (both grippers hovered beside the device's near end for the whole run and never grasped the ankle or touched either slider; the foot stayed 25 mm out of the heel cup); demo: 1.0
